title: Lift a crate on two fork bars only when both are fully under it, and keep it level
instruction: Move the brown crate from the floor bearers onto the blue rack using only the two grey fork bars: slide both bars into the crate's fork pockets until their rear ends reach the white lines, lift the crate level on both bars together, set it on the rack's bearers and slide the bars out. Never lift with a bar less than two-thirds in, tilt the crate more than 5 degrees, raise its bottom above 9.5 cm, drop it or touch it with a gripper. Then put the bars down and let go.
context: Forklift operators, whose training OSHA requires (29 CFR 1910.178(l)), are taught to drive the forks fully under a load before lifting it: a load lifted on the fork tips overloads them and slides or tips off. The load then travels low and level, is set down before the forks are withdrawn, and is never pushed or steadied by hand. Done by industrial truck and tractor operators and hand material movers (O*NET 53-7051.00, 53-7062.00). Here the forks are two loose bars, one in each gripper, and the load is a crate wider than either gripper opens on every side, so it can only be lifted on the bars, by both arms at once and in step: one bar alone lifts one side and tilts it, a bar only part way in leaves the load on its tips. Every lift is checked at every moment, not only where the crate ends up.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Everything has its sides parallel to x and y. (1) Floor bearers: three dark grey timbers fixed to the table, 3.6 cm tall, each from x 27.0 to 38.0 cm: a centre bearer from y -10.0 to +10.0 cm and two outer bearers from y +14.0 to +16.0 cm and from y -14.0 to -16.0 cm. The two 4 cm gaps between them, centred on y +12.0 and -12.0 cm, are the crate's fork pockets; the table is their floor and they are open at both ends. (2) Crate: a loose, closed, empty crate of thin brown plywood, 11.0 cm along x, 30.0 cm along y and 5.0 cm tall, 150 g, resting square on the floor bearers, centred at x 32.5 cm, y 0: its underside is 3.6 cm up, its front face (toward the arms) is at x 27.0 cm, and it covers 1 cm of each outer bearer. (3) Two fork bars: loose grey square aluminium tubes (1.5 mm wall), 16.0 cm long and 2.4 x 2.4 cm in section, 60 g each, lying flat on the table along x, centred at x 19.0 cm, y +12.0 cm and y -12.0 cm, each in line with a pocket: their tips at the pocket mouths (x 27.0 cm), their rear ends at x 11.0 cm. In a pocket a bar has 8 mm of play each side and 12 mm under the crate. (4) Lines: four tape marks 1 mm thick, 1.0 cm along x and 3.0 cm along y, fixed on the table beside the bars' paths at y +17.0 and -17.0 cm: white ones centred at x 21.0 cm (a bar's rear end level with its white line puts its tip 10.0 cm into its pocket: fully in) and yellow ones at x 18.3 cm (7.3 cm in: two-thirds). (5) Rack: a fixed blue-painted wooden platform 3.6 cm tall, from x 40.0 to 55.0 cm and y -17.0 to +17.0 cm, carrying three fixed darker blue wooden bearers 3.6 cm tall in the floor bearers' plan (centre y -10.0 to +10.0 cm, outer y +14.0 to +16.0 cm and -14.0 to -16.0 cm), each from x 41.0 to 52.0 cm, so their tops are 7.2 cm up and the gaps between them leave room to slide the bars out from under a crate set on them. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The scorer watches the whole trial: every control step it reads the crate, both bars and, from the embodiment's state, each gripper's tool point, finger-tip point (between the tips) and opening (0 closed, 1 fully open with the fingers 94 mm apart). A bar's 'insertion' is the length of its centre line under the crate's outline, in the crate's frame, counted while that stretch of the line is within 15 mm (across) of one of the crate's two pocket lines (12.0 cm either side of its centre) and the bar is just under the crate (its centre below the crate's underside, its top no more than 20 mm below it); a pocket's insertion is the larger of the two bars' there. The crate is 'lifted' when its lowest point is more than 3 mm above the tops of the bearers it stands over: the rack's (7.2 cm) once its centre is at or past x 40.0 cm, else the floor bearers' (3.6 cm). 'Tilt' is the angle between the vertical and the axis through the crate's top and bottom (either face down). A gripper 'touches' the crate when any point within 24 mm of the segment from its finger-tip point to 38 mm back up the gripper is within 5 mm of the crate (24 mm reaches the outer corners of fingers closed on a bar whatever the gripper's turn, which is not read). Score 0 if at any moment, whatever happens afterwards: the crate is lifted while either pocket's insertion is under 73 mm; it tilts more than 5 degrees; its lowest point is more than 9.5 cm above the table; its lowest point drops faster than 0.25 m/s (dropped or fell); it leaves the table (its lowest point more than 10 mm below the table top); or a gripper touches it. 'On the rack' means the crate's outline seen from above lies within x 40.0 to 53.0 cm and within 16.5 cm of y 0, its lowest point is within 3 mm of the rack bearers' tops, it is tilted no more than 3 degrees and turned no more than 5 degrees from its start (either way round). Otherwise: 1.0 if the crate is on the rack, every lift was made with both pockets' insertions at least 95 mm, both bars lie wholly outside the crate's outline seen from above, and both grippers have let go (opening 0.9 or more, tool and finger-tip points at least 30 mm from the bars and the crate); 0.75 if the crate is on the rack but not all of that (lifted at some moment with an insertion of 73 to 95 mm, a bar left under it, or a gripper not let go); 0.5 if at some moment the crate was lifted at least 20 mm above the floor bearers with both insertions at least 73 mm and its centre at least 50 mm toward the rack from its start, but it is not on the rack; 0.25 if both insertions were at least 95 mm at the same moment; 0 in every other case. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0. The score is read at the last step: the trial ends early once the 1.0 conditions have held with the crate and both bars still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s) for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit. On a step where the grippers cannot be read, the touch rule is not applied and 'let go' is taken as met. In a real trial: a bubble level on the crate, a 9.5 cm mark behind the rack, and top and side video for the moment-by-moment rules.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, all with the simulator's default friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Rigid bars stand in for forks and a rigid empty crate for the load, about 1:10 scale: no fork deflection, no pallet slats. The bearers, lines and rack are fixed. Only the grippers' fingers are checked for touching the crate, not the rest of each arm, and their heading is not read.
reset_notes: Put the crate back square on the floor bearers, centred at x 32.5 cm, y 0 (front face at x 27.0 cm), and each bar back flat on the table along x, centred at x 19.0 cm, y +12.0 cm and y -12.0 cm, tips at the pocket mouths. Nothing is consumed.
